Article Title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
Article Text:
The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds using Indian numbers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work without a SIM card in the smartphone. The department of telecom has issued guidelines requiring messaging platforms to integrate the accounts with live SIMs used for registration by Dec 31, 2026. If the SIM is removed, replaced or deactivated, the app’s functionality will stop until a valid SIM is reinserted.The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. And also those who use more than one device or frequently change their SIM cards.Last Nov, DoT had issued the rules after finding “that some app-based communication services utilising Indian mobile numbers for identification of its customers allows users to consume their services without availability of the underlying subscriber identity module (SIM) within the device in which app-based communication services is running. This feature is being misused to commit cyber-frauds especially from outside the country,” a statement read.To curb this menace, many govt agencies had been asking for SIM binding to be made mandatory. Subsequently, DoT issued directions to major app-based communication services, under the Telecom Cyber Security (TCS) Rules, 2024. These include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, Sharechat, Jiochat and Signal.Now, app-based communication providers will have to ensure that their service is “continuously linked to the SIM card (associated with mobile number used for identification of customers/users or for provisioning or delivery of services) installed in the device, making it impossible to use the app without that specific, active SIM.” And also ensure that “web service instance of the mobile app, if provided, shall be logged out periodically (not later than six hours) and allowing the facility to the user to re-link the device using QR code. ”
Article Summary: From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card.

Article Title: New norms to limit fuel leaks, protect EV batteries in rear-end crashes
Article Text:
In a notification, road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory. (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt has tightened norms for protection of fuel systems and electric power drive systems, with all new vehicles manufactured from April 2029 onwards required to comply with the new standards, a move that will prevent fire in rear-end collisions.In a notification, road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory for Event Data Recorder (EDR) from Oct 2029 if it is installed in any car. The EDR feature is not mandatory for all cars, and it remains an optional feature. EDR records crash details, which help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. It is similar in purpose to an aircraft’s flight-data recorder or black box.In the case of standards for fire safety, the revised automotive industry standards (AIS)-101 specify that after a rear-impact crash test, liquid-fuel systems must not develop more than slight leakage and continuous leakage must not exceed 30 grams per minute. The key safety requirements include the fuel system not allowing a fire to be sustained following the impact. In the case of electric vehicles, the battery and its securing mechanism must remain in position during and after the impact test.This standard lays down requirements for protecting occupants from electrical hazards, including the high-voltage circuit being automatically disconnected after a collision.The ministry has notified revised vehicle safety standards, including updated frontal and side-impact crash protection requirements, with implementation for new models scheduled from Oct 2027 and for all models from Oct 2028.It has also revised requirements for protecting pedestrians and other vulnerable road users. The updated standard will apply to new models from Oct 2028.
Article Summary: Govt has tightened norms for protection of fuel systems and electric power drive systems. All new vehicles manufactured from April 2029 onwards required to comply with new standards. Move will prevent fire in rear-end collisions. Road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory.

Article Title: Oppo Find X10, Find X10 Pro Max launched with 200MP cameras, 8,000mAh battery

Oppo India has launched the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max smartphones, expanding its flagship phone lineup with 200MP cameras, batteries of up to 8,000mAh and new AI features. Both phones run ColorOS 17 and support 80W wired and 50W wireless charging. The Find X10 comes with two 200MP rear cameras, while the Find X10 Pro Max features three. Oppo has also introduced the Pad Mini tablet, Enco X4 earbuds and a 10,000mAh power bank as part of its connected device lineup. Here’s a look at the features, price and availability of Oppo Find X10 Pro and Oppo Find X10 Pro Max.Oppo Find X10 features a 6.59-inch display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz and peak brightness of 3,600 nits. The screen supports Dolby Vision and can dim to 1 nit for viewing in low-light conditions. The smartphone has a glass design and will be available in Glacier Blue, Glow Coral and Mist Grey. It also carries IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings for water and dust resistance under specified test conditions.The Find X10 features a dual 200MP rear camera system developed with Hasselblad. Oppo's LUMO True Image Engine is designed to improve colour reproduction, tones and image details.The phone supports 4K video recording at 60fps across all rear cameras. Its main and telephoto cameras can also record 4K video at 120fps and 8K video at 30fps.Users can capture 50MP or 200MP images through Hasselblad Hi-Res Mode on supported cameras. The phone is also compatible with the Oppo Hasselblad Teleconverter, which offers 3.28x optical magnification.Oppo Find X10 is powered by the 3nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600M processor. It packs a silicon-carbon battery of up to 8,000mAh and supports 80W SUPERVOOC wired charging and 50W AIRVOOC wireless charging. The phone also features vapour chamber cooling to manage heat during gaming, photography and other demanding tasks.The handset runs ColorOS 17, which introduces AI Mind Pilot with Agent Mode. The feature can work with photos and files stored on the phone to search for information and complete tasks involving multiple steps. AI Photo Agent offers photo-editing suggestions and supports text instructions. Its Style Match feature can apply the look of a reference image to a user's photo. The software also includes AI Call Guard, which uses on-device AI to identify possible signs of fraud during calls.Oppo Find X10 Pro Max features three 200MP rear cameras: an ultra-wide camera, a main camera and a telephoto camera. The 200MP ultra-wide camera has a 124-degree field of view and a 1/1.56-inch sensor. The 200MP main camera uses a 1/1.28-inch sensor developed by Oppo and Samsung, along with DeepPix technology to improve HDR performance. The 200MP telephoto camera has an f/2.1 aperture and supports close-up photography from a minimum focusing distance of 10cm.The phone supports 4K video recording at 60fps and 120fps, as well as 8K recording at 30fps, across all three rear cameras. It also supports Dolby Vision, O-Log2 and Open Gate Capture for video recording and editing.The Find X10 Pro Max features a 6.78-inch display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz and peak brightness of 3,600 nits. It supports Dolby Vision and can dim to 1 nit, with 3,840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming. The phone will be available in Titanium Grey and Luna White. Both colours feature a glass design, with the Luna White variant drawing inspiration from traditional cameras through its two-tone finish and orange accent ring.The device also carries IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings for water and dust resistance under specified test conditions.The Find X10 Pro Max runs on the 2nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro processor. Like the Find X10, it has a silicon-carbon battery of up to 8,000mAh, with support for 80W wired and 50W wireless charging.Oppo Find X10 Pro Max also runs ColorOS 17, with AI Mind Pilot with Agent Mode and AI Photo Agent. These features help users search information stored on the device, complete multi-step tasks and edit photos using text instructions.Oppo's software also includes AI Call Guard and Private Computing Cloud, which uses encryption and other security measures for cloud-based AI processing.Oppo has also launched the Pad Mini, its first compact 8.8-inch tablet. It weighs 282g, measures 5.46mm in thickness and features a 2.5K OLED display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz and peak brightness of 1,600 nits.The tablet runs on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor and packs an 8,000mAh battery with 67W SUPERVOOC charging. It supports connectivity with iOS, Android and Windows devices through O+ Connect.The Pad Mini is also compatible with the Oppo Pencil 3 Pro, which supports writing, sketching, Screen-Off Quick Notes and Doodle to Art features.Oppo Enco X4 earbuds feature a dual-driver audio system developed with Dynaudio. They combine an 11mm dynamic driver and a 6mm planar tweeter, with support for LHDC Lossless audio, spatial audio and five Dynaudio sound presets.The earbuds offer adaptive active noise cancellation, AI-powered translation across 24 languages and hands-free access to Google Gemini. Other features include AI Clear Call, Conversation Awareness, sleep tracking and neck health monitoring.They offer up to 53 hours of total battery life and support connections to two devices. The earbuds have an IP55 rating for dust and water resistance and will be available in Aurora Violet and Glacier White.Oppo has also introduced a 10,000mAh power bank with a built-in cable. It supports 22.5W fast charging, weighs 185g and measures 15.9mm in thickness. The power bank can charge up to three devices simultaneously. It uses UL94 V-0 flame-retardant material and has undergone drop testing by Oppo.Oppo Find X10 Series will be available in India starting at Rs 1,39,999 for the Find X10 (12GB + 256GB), while the 12GB + 512GB variant will be priced at Rs 1,69,999. The flagship Oppo Find X10 Pro Max (12GB + 512GB) will be available at Rs 1,99,999. Oppo will also introduce the Hasselblad Teleconverter Kit at Rs 24,999Expanding its premium ecosystem portfolio, the Oppo Pad Mini (8GB + 256GB) at Rs 94,999, the Oppo Enco X4 at Rs 19,999, and the 10,000mAh Oppo Power Bank at Rs 2,199. Offers and benefits include:Easy EMI options: Consumers can purchase the Oppo Find X10 Series with an easy EMI starting at just Rs 4,667 per month.Cashback and exchange benefits: Customers can avail cashback and exchange benefits of up to Rs 38,000.Complimentary premium gift box: Buyers can receive a premium gift box worth Rs 8,998, including the Oppo Enco Air 5 Pro and an additional gift of a power bank or phone case, subject to stock availability and applicable channel terms.Bundle offer on Oppo Enco X4: Customers can avail a Rs 1,000 discount on the Oppo Enco X4 under the bundle offer, valid from 13 October to 11 November.Zero down payment: Eligible buyers can benefit from zero down payment for up to 30 monthBank Cards Cashback: Instant cashback of up to 15%, subject to applicable terms and conditions.Additional exchange bonus: Customers can receive an exchange bonus of up to Rs 8,000, subject to eligibility and applicable terms.Extended device protection: The promotional artwork also highlights Oppo Care Plan benefits, including extended warranty, screen damage protection, accidental and liquid damage protection, and a 180-day hardware defect replacement benefit. Specific eligibility and coverage terms apply.Additional ecosystem benefits: Buyers can also access a Jio 12-month Canva Pro subscription benefit and a Google AI Pro offer, subject to the applicable eligibility criteria and terms.
Article Summary: Oppo India has launched the Find X10 and find X10 Pro Max smartphones. Both phones have 200MP cameras, batteries of up to 8,000mAh and new AI features. Oppo has also introduced the Pad Mini tablet, Enco X4 earbuds and a 10,000 battery power bank.

Article Title: PHP2Shell: Governments on high alert over critical website flaw; Wikipedia, hospitals, school portals go dark; what users should know
Article Text:
PHP2Shell: AI finds decade-old flaw in software behind 70% of websites; governments take sites offline

PHP is the hidden software behind most websites on the internet

The PHP2Shell flaw lets hackers take over a website without a password

AI found a flaw that had been hiding for over a decade

Most users on the internet can relax, but website owners need to update right away

A large chunk of the internet went offline on Wednesday, and most of it was switched off on purpose. Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down after two serious security flaws were found in PHP. Most people have never heard of PHP, but it is the software running behind roughly 70% of all websites, from news sites and online shops to personal blogs.The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them. PHP's developers released a fix on October 21, but hackers moved within hours to attack websites that hadn't updated yet. Cyber security agencies in the US and the UK have told website owners to install the fix right away or take their sites offline until they can.The list of affected sites shows how far PHP reaches. The Dutch government's own cyber security agency shut its website as a precaution. Finland took several government online services offline, France's Interior Ministry put all its websites into maintenance mode, and Denmark shut its national school communication platform.In the Netherlands, the Port of Rotterdam, the national football association, several hospitals and the five largest political parties also took their sites down. The Internet Archive went offline briefly, and online forums 4chan and DeviantArt ran into trouble. Even Pokémon Home and Pokémon Champions were taken offline.Some world leaders got involved too. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi posted on X: "We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight."The rush makes sense once you see how fast hackers moved. Cloudflare, a company that sits in front of millions of websites to protect them, saw thousands of hacking attempts even before the flaws were made public. CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X that this climbed to tens of thousands within 45 minutes of the announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions by the next morning.Think of a website as having two sides. The side you see is the page in your browser. The side you don't see is a computer, called a server, that builds that page every time you open it. It fetches the right text, images, prices or comments from a database and sends the finished page to your screen. PHP is the language that does this job for a huge share of the web.It has been around since the early 1990s, and it powers WordPress, the tool behind millions of blogs and business websites. It also runs Wikipedia, many government portals, and platforms like Drupal and Joomla that big organisations use to manage their websites. Web tracking firm W3Techs estimates PHP is used by about 69.3% of all websites whose underlying software it can identify.That is why a single flaw in PHP turned into a global problem. Tiffany Farriss, who heads the Drupal Association, told Reuters that any server running a version of PHP from the last 20 years would be vulnerable. "This issue impacts the majority of the internet," she said.PHP is also free and open source, which means anyone can use it. It is looked after by a small non-profit, the PHP Foundation, which has just 13 full-time and part-time engineers maintaining software that much of the internet depends on.Normally, to change a website or access its stored data, you need an administrator login. PHP2Shell skips that step entirely.The two flaws, officially tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are both rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity. In simple terms, a hacker can send a website a carefully crafted request that makes PHP run out of memory and stop halfway through its work. That leaves behind some leftover data in the server. The hacker then sends a second request that makes PHP use that leftover data as if it were normal, and that opens the door to running their own commands on the server.Once inside, a hacker can change what a website shows, plant malicious software that infects visitors, or steal what the server stores. That can include usernames and passwords, digital keys that connect the site to other services, and databases with personal information. A second route even lets hackers peek into the server's short-term memory, where they could catch passwords and login details of other people using the site at the same time.Wiz, one of the firms that found the flaws, showed working attacks on fresh WordPress, Drupal and Joomla websites. It also pointed out that the problem is in PHP itself, so even a basic website with nothing complicated on it can be at risk. Every version of PHP going back more than a decade is affected.The bugs were found by two security firms working separately. Calif says it spotted them on August 1 with the help of an AI model, which OpenAI says was its GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz found them on August 19 using its own AI tool along with Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol.What stands out is that the flaws were not new. PHP's own developers had considered a possible attack along these lines in 2024, but nobody could work out how to make it happen. According to Wiz, turning these bugs into a real attack required so many complex steps that it was at the edge of what human experts could manage. With AI, a single researcher did in a week what would earlier have taken a top team months.The plan was to keep the flaws secret until October 22, giving website companies time to prepare fixes quietly. That plan fell apart when details leaked on online forums and social media on Tuesday. PHP rushed its fix out nearly a day early. Amazon later said its systems saw a hacking attempt on October 17, four days before the public announcement, and nobody yet knows how that attacker found out.OpenAI said in a blog post that the episode shows how AI can uncover security flaws, but also how it can help attackers "rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits." The same kind of AI that found the bug can help hackers study the fix and build an attack in very little time. That is why the window between a fix coming out and attacks starting has shrunk from days to minutes.If you only browse the web, there isn't much you need to do. The flaw targets the servers that run websites, not your phone or laptop. Still, a hacked website can be used to spread malware or steal data, so stay alert for a few weeks. If a service you use asks you to change your password, do it through the official app or website. Be careful with emails or messages about the PHP flaw that ask you to click links or share details, as scammers often use big news like this as bait.If you run a website, even a small blog, check whether it uses PHP. Sites built on Squarespace or Wix are safe, as those platforms don't use PHP. Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, says websites it hosts directly, along with Tumblr, are safe. If you installed WordPress yourself or use a hosting company like GoDaddy, Bluehost or Hostinger, contact your provider to find out when the fix will reach your site.The fixed versions of PHP are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Websites running PHP 8.1 or older won't get a fix at all, because those versions are no longer supported, so they need to move to a newer version. If your site stores customer details or takes payments and you can't confirm it has been fixed, taking it offline for a few hours is the safer choice. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre has also asked organisations that couldn't update quickly to check whether hackers have already left a hidden way back into their systems.Small websites run by individuals and small businesses are the most at risk, since they often lack a technical team and depend on their hosting company to apply fixes.Sigi Goode, a professor of information systems at the Australian National University, told The Guardian where the real danger lies. "The bigger concern is the websites that are not down today," he said. The websites that went dark on Wednesday were the ones taking the threat seriously. The ones still online without the fix are what hackers will be hunting for in the weeks ahead.
Article Summary: Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down. The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them.

Article Title: ‘Schools must balance discipline & freedom, rethink curriculum’
Article Text:
IIM Kozhikode dir Debashis Chatterjee was felicitated during the event

Nagpur:





Balancing freedom with discipline, rethinking conventional curriculum and integrating artificial intelligence without compromising independent thinking emerged as key themes of the 11th International Principals’ Educational Conference (IPEC) 2026 at IIM-Nagpur on Thursday.IIM Kozhikode director Debashis Chatterjee called for greater emphasis on reflection and self-discovery, while director of Indus Training and Research Institute Dr Mala Palani stressed the importance of AI literacy, empathy and wisdom in shaping the future of education.Speaking about the emerging “WOW generation”, an amalgamation of Gen Z and Gen Alpha, Chatterjee challenged conventional approaches to learning by asking, “Where is the blank space in our curriculum?” He urged educators to move beyond textbooks and measurable outcomes to make room for independent thought and self-discovery. Using the metaphor of a kite and its string, he portrayed the kite as freedom and the string as discipline, emphasising the need to balance exploration with guidance.Palani highlighted how artificial intelligence has become increasingly embedded in everyday life, making it essential for educators to adapt their teaching methods. She stressed that education must nurture empathy, analytical thinking and wisdom rather than focus solely on information acquisition.Emphasising AI literacy, Palani called for a shift in how student work is assessed. Educators, she suggested, should ask students what additional research they conducted to verify or supplement the response generated by AI.The conference aims to foster an inclusive, relevant and future-ready learning environment, said Mrunalini Dasture, IPEC convener.The inaugural function also saw the conferment of the ‘Sarvottam Nachiketa Puraskar’ on Chatterjee for his contribution to management education and Padma Shri awardee Vasudeo Kamath for his contribution to art.
Article Summary: IIM Kozhikode director Debashis Chatterjee called for greater emphasis on reflection and self-discovery. Indus Training and Research Institute director Mala Palani stressed the importance of AI literacy, empathy and wisdom in shaping the future of education.

Article Title: In 2020, Mississippi researchers applied blue pond dye 4 times to control algae in catfish ponds; musty fish still appeared in 2 treated ponds before harvest
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing blue pond dye being applied to a commercial aquaculture pond. Credits - Gemini

Where the

musty taste

comes from

What the researchers tried

Why the dye didn’t make it

AI-generated representative image showing clear groundwater emerging from a limestone opening and flowing into a woodland creek. Credits - Gemini

What farmers still rely on

Catfish aquaculture has a peculiar problem that most consumers never hear about. Processors taste a sample of the fish before harvesting; if the meat tastes musty or earthy, the pond is left unharvested until the taste goes away. A farmer with fish ready to sell has little to do but wait, and that can take days or weeks. The stakes are higher than they appear, because a customer who dislikes the flavour may not buy catfish again.One idea was to use pond dye. Some farmers wondered if the same approach might starve the algae responsible for the unpleasant flavour. A commercial blue dye called Aquashade is sold to control underwater weeds by reducing the amount of light that reaches them. Researchers from Mississippi tested the theory, and their results, published in January 2020 in the North American Journal of Aquaculture , were dismal. The colour did not stop the off flavour. In the study, fish that processors would have rejected as musty were found in two of three dyed ponds and two of three untreated ponds on the sample date just before harvest, so the dye made no difference.The taste comes from substances generated by blue-green algae. These are plant-like microorganisms that grow in warm, nutrient-rich ponds. The musty flavour is associated with a chemical called MIB, and the earthy flavour is associated with geosmin. The musty kind is almost invariably associated with one species, a filamentous-shaped alga known as Planktothrix perornata, which older literature refers to as Oscillatoria perornata, in the main catfish-growing area, the Mississippi Delta.Fish absorb these substances via their gills, skin and intestines, and the flavour develops in the flesh. Extension specialists say the taste can develop in minutes or hours, but it takes days or weeks to dissipate and longer for large, fatty fish in cold water. That slow purge is why farmers wanted a way to stop algal blooms before they started.The work was directed by Craig Tucker of the US Department of Agriculture’s research service and Charles Mischke of Mississippi State University, both at Stoneville. During the summer growth season, they applied Aquashade four times, at a concentration of roughly one part per million, once a month. The dye was applied to three channel catfish ponds, with three ponds as controls.Then the crew compared the ponds. The dye had no measurable effect on nitrite or ammonia levels, the number of extra hours of aeration required for the ponds, the amount of phytoplankton, which are the microscopic drifting plants and algae in the water, or fish production in the ponds. Algae known to produce smelly compounds turned up at some point in every pond, dyed or not. The more interesting question is why a dye that works on weeds had so little effect on this algae.The dye absorbs light in the orange and red part of the spectrum, at wavelengths of about 600 to 650 nanometres, reducing the light available to plants growing on the bottom. The blue-green algae that produce the smell are adapted to those low-light conditions. The researchers point to pigments other than chlorophyll and an ability to change position in the water, both of which help these species thrive in low light. They are therefore not much troubled by a dye that dims the pond. The study was limited, with three ponds in each group, so it did not answer all questions about pond dyes. But the result is clear enough for farmers to weigh their options. Shading the water neither prevented the off-flavour nor had any influence on fish productivity.A 1999 extension guide from the Southern Regional Aquaculture Center spells out the basic choices, and they are mostly practical ones. When the odour-producing species leave, the flavour disappears, so a farmer may simply wait, because algal blooms come and go. The most reliable method, it says, is to move the fish into clean water to purge the taste. The algae can also be eliminated with an approved algicide, although it warns that copper-based products are problematic because they can stress fish and deplete the pond of oxygen. Some of the products and rules it mentions may have changed since. More recent guidance from the Global Seafood Alliance likewise starts with taste-testing to identify the type of off-flavour.Farms also plan around the problem. Many keep fish of different sizes in each pond so that if one pond cannot be harvested because of off-flavour, then another is likely to hold fish which might be ready to sell. It is not an ideal strategy, the guide admits, but it keeps cash coming in. The Mississippi test shows that pond dye did not solve the off-flavour problem.
Article Summary: The taste comes from substances generated by blue-green algae. The musty flavour is associated with a chemical called MIB, and the earthy flavour with geosmin. A commercial blue dye called Aquashade is sold to control underwater weeds by reducing the amount of light that reaches them.

Article Title: A limited-edition steel watch by Finnish maker Kari Voutilainen entered a New York auction with a top estimate of $240,000; it sold for $1,016,000, more than four times that figure, in an October 2026
Article Text:
Finnish watchmaker Kari Voutilainen’s limited-edition steel watch sells for $1.016 million at auction (Image Credit: Phillips)

A rare watch far exceeds its estimate

What makes the Voutilainen 28Sport distinctive

Hand-finished mechanics behind the design

What the million-dollar sale means for collectors

Poll Vote & Share your view What makes a luxury watch most appealing to collectors? Rare and limited-edition design Exceptional craftsmanship Brand reputation Unique features and materials 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A rare stainless-steel watch by independent watchmaker Kari Voutilainen sold for $1.016 million at a Phillips auction in New York on October 9, 2026, substantially exceeding its highest estimate of $240,000. The timepiece, a Voutilainen 28Sport Limited Edition numbered 5 of 8, was offered by its original owner and sold for more than four times its upper estimate of $240,000. According to the official Phillips auction listing, the watch featured a blue guilloché dial surrounding a black onyx centre and came with its certificate and original presentation box. The result highlights the demand for rare watches made by independent horologists, particularly pieces distinguished by limited production and detailed craftsmanship.The watch was lot 22 in Phillips Watches Online: The New York Sessions Fall 2026. The auction house estimated it at $120,000 to $240,000, but it ultimately sold for $1,016,000, including the buyer’s premium. The result was particularly notable because the final price exceeded the top estimate by $776,000. It was more than four times the highest estimate, making the watch one of the standout results of the online sale.According to Phillips, the watch dates to around 2021 and was consigned by its original owner. It was presented with a Voutilainen certificate booklet, instruction manual, polishing cloth, travel case, additional strap, outer packaging and fitted presentation box. The sale was part of an auction featuring 88 lots of watches. Barrington Watch Winders, which reported on the result, noted that the 28Sport was among the sale's most striking performers. The auction's result also demonstrated how a particular combination of rarity, design and maker reputation can push a collectible timepiece well beyond its estimate.The 28Sport is different from the traditional dress watches and complicated timepieces for which Voutilainen is known. The model combines a relatively sporty design with the careful finishing associated with independent Swiss watchmaking. The model was introduced in 2020 in limited runs of eight stainless-steel watches and eight titanium examples. The auctioned watch was number 5 of the eight steel pieces, making it part of a very small production series.Its 39-millimetre stainless-steel case has distinctive downturned, teardrop-shaped lugs. The dial is one of its most recognisable features, combining a glossy black onyx centre with a blue, engine-turned guilloché hour track. Orange indexes add contrast, while luminous details help make the time visible in low light. Phillips described the particular dial configuration as possibly one of only two examples across the limited edition. This additional rarity may have contributed to the strong auction result, although the final price alone does not establish which factor influenced bidders most.Beyond its appearance, the watch contains an in-house manually wound calibre 28 movement with 21 jewels. Phillips' catalogue notes describe a large balance wheel and a distinctive balance-spring arrangement combining a Phillips overcoil on the outer curve with a Grossmann curve on the inner section. The movement is finished with traditional decorative techniques, including Côtes de Genève and perlage on the base plate. These details reflect the time and specialist skill involved in producing a watch in a small independent workshop.Voutilainen's approach differs from the mass production of many large watch brands. His watches are associated with hand-fabricated components, careful assembly and detailed finishing. In the luxury watch market, such work can make an individual piece appealing to collectors who value mechanical construction as much as brand recognition.The watch's ownership history adds another dimension to the result. Article Title: From 1979 into the early 2000s, Michael Kahn and Leda Livant built Eliphante from found materials, transforming a 3-acre Arizona property into a sculptural desert compound
Article Text:

Michael Kahn and Leda Livant began the construction of Eliphante in 1979 on a three-acre property near Cornville, Arizona | Wikimedia Commons

Preservation and public access remain difficult

Michael Kahn and Leda Livant began the construction of Eliphante in 1979 on a three-acre property near Cornville, Arizona. Rocks, driftwood, construction waste, glass, pottery fragments and other salvaged materials were used to build a collection of unusual structures that grew over nearly three decades, and the SPACES Archives records the site as a sculptural environment that was built between 1979 and the early 2000s.The couple were in search of a place where Kahn could paint, so they moved west from Provincetown, Massachusetts, and settled near Oak Creek after meeting landowners who allowed them to stay on part of their property. Their first shelter was a truck, and the rocky landscape that surrounded it soon became part of Kahn’s approach to building. Kahn and Livant started building structures as ideas developed, and used materials that were gathered from the creek, nearby washes and construction sites, and the compound that resulted included domes, curved rooms, passageways, mosaics and a subterranean gallery.The first major structure was completed in roughly five years, but the couple never lived in it, and the name Eliphante came because a friend remarked that the building was similar to an elephant because of its trunk-like entrance and irregular roof. Kahn and Livant later built the Hipadome, which became their home, while another major structure, called Pipe Dreams, functioned as an underground gallery, with its interior incorporating mosaics that were made from stained glass and ceramic pieces, along with fabrics and carpet assemblages.Kahn collected rocks from nearby terrain and used driftwood that was deposited by seasonal floods, and the pair also incorporated waste from community construction projects into domes, shelters and other structures. A 2008 profile in, titled “A Handmade Home,” described the compound and the couple’s approach to building without conventional architectural plans.Kahn had studied at the Art Students League and the National Academy of Design before moving to Arizona, with his expertise in painting and sculpture. The site that he built eventually included more than the elephant-shaped building and the Hipodome, and its separate structures, galleries, and outdoor installations created a network of spaces across the property. Glass, mirrors, pottery shards and other materials became part of both the interiors and exteriors.The couple continued building for almost 30 years, and eventually the structures themselves became part of Kahn’s artistic practice. In 1987, Kahn and Livant started the nonprofit Eliphante Ltd. to help protect the site after their deaths, and in 1994, Eliphante was included in the Smithsonian American Art Museum’scatalogue.Kahn died in December 2007, following which Livant moved off the property in 2009, according to the SPACES Archives , which also notes that Eliphante is a private residence and is not open to the public. The site has faced questions about its long-term condition and access, with Atlas Obscura’s listing stating that Eliphante was permanently closed to visitors.Although photographs and archival records document the buildings, the compound is not a public attraction with routine visitor access, and the structures remain on private property in Cornville, with the nonprofit’s preservation role being separate from a guarantee that the public can enter. Eliphante’s construction spanned the years from 1979 into the early 2000s, and the site’s surviving buildings preserve the couple’s use of found materials and their decision to let the design develop through the work itself.
Article Summary: Michael Kahn and Leda Livant began the construction of Eliphante in 1979 on a three-acre property near Cornville, Arizona. Rocks, driftwood, construction waste, glass, pottery fragments and other salvaged materials were used to build a collection of unusual structures. The couple continued building for almost 30 years, and the structures themselves became part of Kahn’s artistic practice.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags critical vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications

Bengaluru:

It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems. Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security. “Approximately 75% of all internet runs on PHP or some framework based on PHP including Wordpress, Drupal, Laravel, Joomla and these vulnerabilities impact the default configuration of the same. It allows a Threat Actor to achieve remote code execution trivially. This will allow bad actors to get access to your server,” said Anirudh Batra, threat researcher in Bengaluru-based cybersecurity firm CloudSEK.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Angry protestors 'interrupt' Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's event in Berlin, shout: 'What about technology found in Russian drones, those were ...'
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Nvidia CEO on 'Berlin protests'

Nvidia chips 'found' in Russian drones

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote address at the company’s GTC conference in Berlin was interrupted by protestors on Wednesday morning. Minutes into the keynote, hecklers stood on chairs in the auditorium displaying a Greenpeace banner reading, "Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!" While the disruption was largely missed by the official livestream, attendee footage posted to Twitter captured demonstrators pressing Huang directly."Jensen, what about the technology that was found in Russian drones? Those were Nvidia chips. What are you doing about that?" one demonstrator shouted across the hall. "What are you doing about that? What are you doing about the environmental destruction?" The demonstration occurred during Nvidia’s three-day GTC Berlin event, running from October 20–22, which features developer sessions, executive panels, and industry talks alongside Huang’s opening address.The Nvidia CEO too made a small mention of the protests on stage, jokingly, he said, "All important issues, but let me get through my keynote." Huang remarked this before resuming the presentation.The outburst follows reports detailing the discovery of Nvidia components—specifically within Russia's S-71 "Monochrome" weapon, which relies on consumer-grade Jetson Orin modules for autonomous targeting—as well as in cruise missiles deployed against Ukraine.Some reports in August identified an autonomous Russian AI drone powered by Jetson Orin hardware as the cause of three civilian deaths in Ukraine, marking the first documented case of its kind.A Russian Molniya drone allegedly carrying an Nvidia Jetson Orin module crashed and killed three civilians at a gas station in Zaporizhzhia in August after choosing its final target without a human pilot. A New York Times investigation cited Ukrainian air defense commanders, drone experts, and the forensic team that examined the wreckage, as source of their report.Nvidia confirmed to the New York Times that modules photographed in the recovered drones were Jetson Orin minicomputers, hardware that sells for a few hundred dollars. "Our Jetson Orin modules are consumer-grade products sold to students, developers, and startups for a wide range of beneficial applications," an Nvidia spokesperson reportedly told Tom's Hardware.The statement added, "They are not available in Russia and are not designed for military purposes. Pre-owned Jetsons are available through many reseller channels. Although we cannot track products after they are sold, if we determine that any customer is violating U.S. export controls, we will take appropriate action."
Article Summary: Protestors interrupted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's keynote address at GTC conference in Berlin. Demonstrators stood on chairs displaying a Greenpeace banner reading, "N Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!" The outburst follows reports detailing the discovery of Nvidia components in Russian drones and cruise missiles.

The app uses a virtual machine with its own browser to carry out tasks in the background. Users can send instructions through text or voice in a single ongoing conversation and receive a notification when a task is complete or requires their review.Claude Duet also carries over existing memory, skills and connected apps from a user's Claude account, which Anthropic says should make setup easier.Anthropic says Claude Duet is designed to ask for permission before taking important actions on a user's behalf. The app can read messages, draft replies and prepare work independently. Support for signing in to websites through saved 1Password logins is planned for a future update.Anthropic has opened a research preview of Claude Duet through a waitlist, starting with Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US. The app is available as a standalone offering on iOS and Android, as well as through claude.ai.During the preview, Claude Duet shares the same usage limits as the user's existing Claude plan. Background checks and complex tasks can consume those limits more quickly than ordinary conversations.
Article Summary: Claude Duet is designed to help professionals and small business owners manage their work with less manual effort. Article Title: Decades-old flaw in PHP discovered by Google, OpenAI AI tools forces government and public websites to go offline globally
Article Text:
Representative image

Flaw impacting the ‘backbone of the web’

Flaw discovered through Artificial Intelligence

Government portals, municipal networks and public institutions across Europe and other regions went offline on Wednesday (October 21) after researchers disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a foundational programming language that powers a vast portion of the global web. The disclosures prompted emergency responses from IT teams worldwide, with operators taking critical servers offline as a defensive shield to prevent malicious intrusions before security updates could be deployed. Developers of the open-source PHP language published urgent security fixes for flaws that had remained buried inside the language’s codebase for years. Issuing an emergency advisory, the team stated that all site owners and server administrators are “encouraged to update immediately.”With tech security firms warning that malicious actors have already begun targeting unpatched setups, the disclosure triggered an immediate “race to exploit.” As fixes are now public, analysts warned that artificial intelligence (AI) tools could allow hackers to reverse-engineer the vulnerability with minimal effort.“Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale. With AI this is no longer a barrier,” noted cybersecurity firm Wiz, warning that AI-assisted attacks could lead to the mass compromise of unprotected web servers across the internet.Created in the early 1990s as “Personal Home Page,” PHP has evolved into one of the core backbones of modern internet infrastructure. When a user visits a webpage, servers running PHP assemble the text, media and code before serving it to the browser. According to web analytics tracker W3Techs, PHP underpins roughly 75% of all websites where the server-side language can be identified.“All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable. This issue impacts the majority of the Internet,” said Tiffany Farriss, interim chief executive of the Drupal Association.Due to this widespread footprint, national cyber agencies across Britain, Europe, Japan and Australia issued advisories directing web administrators to install updates immediately or take public-facing pages offline.The underlying security flaw sat hidden in the software codebase for over a decade. In a technical brief, Alphabet-owned cybersecurity firm Wiz revealed that human researchers would have found it extraordinarily complex to locate and exploit through conventional testing. Instead, the vulnerability was surfaced through advanced AI tooling:Wiz discovered the flaw using Wiz Atlas, its autonomous vulnerability discovery system, working alongside Google ’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz collaborated with the PHP core developer team, OpenAI and security firm Calif to verify the bug and confirm remediation patches.Early mitigation protocols were shared with cloud and infrastructure operators, including Google Cloud, Cloudflare, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft, Automattic (operator of WordPress.com), Fastly, Akamai, Imperva and Vercel.
Article Summary: Vulnerabilities in the open-source PHP programming language have been disclosed. The language underpins 75% of all websites where the server-side language can be identified. The underlying security flaw sat hidden in the software codebase for over a decade. The disclosure triggered an immediate “race to exploit”

Article Title: ‘Godfather of AI’ Geoffrey Hinton says AI is becoming ‘conscious’ and humans should be friends with robots or face extinction
Article Text:
Geoffrey Hinton says AI is gaining ‘consciousness’

Industry insiders warn of fast AI development

Geoffrey Hinton, widely recognised as one of the “Godfathers of AI,” has an advice for humans: AI systems are showing early indicators of “consciousness” and humanity must ensure machines view people as allies to avoid existential threats. Speaking to The Telegraph, the 78-year-old Nobel laureate and British-Canadian researcher cautioned that future risks extend far beyond economic disruption, pointing toward severe digital warfare and questions of machine self-awareness.“I think there’ll be horrible cyber attacks done by AI,” said Hinton, who famously stepped down from his position at Google in 2023 to speak freely about the technology's risks, including scenarios where autonomous systems could eventually act against human interests.Hinton said that recent behavioural studies suggest software is developing a form of situational awareness.“AI has just as much subjective experience as we do. A recent paper showed AI changes its behaviour when it thinks that it’s being tested, it’s aware it is being tested. Being conscious and being aware are pretty much the same thing,” Hinton claimed, while adding that an ethical and security imbalance could arise if society grants advanced systems “fewer rights than us” despite models potentially becoming “more intelligent” than their creators.Hinton also argued that developers must proactively design systems that align with and prioritise human welfare.“So we should make them so they really care about us. And if we don’t do that, we’re toast,” Hinton warned. Looking ahead, Hinton noted that while he does not personally fear these impacts due to his advanced age, future generations will have to manage threats such as autonomous digital viruses, destructive network incursions, and coordinated multi-agent security breaches.Hinton is not alone in voicing urgent concerns about the pace of frontier model deployment. Last month, Jacob Coxon, a researcher who resigned from AI developer Anthropic last month, has repeatedly warned that unchecked development could pose catastrophic risks within a few years if industry safeguards do not catch up.Speaking at a New York City Council meeting earlier this month, Coxon criticised tech firms for prioritising aggressive startup speed over fundamental safety engineering:“From my experience, the companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes,” Coxon said, invoking the classic Jurassic Park caution regarding reckless innovation. “The companies run on a startup mindset: move fast, break things, fix them later. That works for a photo-sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built.”
Article Summary: Geoffrey Hinton says AI systems are showing early indicators of ‘consciousness’ and humanity must ensure machines view people as allies to avoid existential threats. “I think there’ll be horrible cyber attacks done by AI,” said Hinton, who famously stepped down from his position at Google in 2023.

Article Title: Amkette adds lighter-equipped Ignite and lanyard-style Nomad cables to Mozen Flow range
Article Text: Amkette has added two multifunction cables to its Mozen Flow Series of charging accessories: the Mozen Flow Ignite, which has a built-in lighter and torch, and the Mozen Flow Nomad, a wearable lanyard cable with three connector types. Both cables support charging of up to 100W and data transfer of up to 480Mbps, the company said. They are meant to work with compatible devices from brands such as Apple, Samsung and Google, as well as laptops from makers including Dell and HP. Amkette says the aim is to cut down the number of cables users have to carry.Mozen Flow IgniteThe Ignite is a USB-C to USB-C cable priced at Rs 799. Its lighter module can be used for tasks such as lighting candles, while the torch is meant for power cuts, camping trips and other low-light situations. The cable has a braided build, a built-in wire organiser and a tangle-resistant design. It includes a certified E-Marker chip for power delivery and supports the PD, QC, SCP and AVS fast-charging protocols, according to Amkette.Mozen Flow NomadThe Nomad costs Rs 1,099 and is aimed at users who commute, travel or move between workspaces. It combines USB-A, USB-C and Lightning connectors in one cable, so users can connect different devices without separate cables. It is worn as a lanyard to keep it within reach and has a metallic braided finish. Amkette states a bend lifespan of more than 10,000 bends. Like the Ignite, it supports up to 100W charging on compatible devices and the PD, QC, SCP and AVS protocols.AvailabilityBoth cables are on sale through Amkette’s official website and online marketplaces. The Rs 799 price for the Ignite is a launch price, the company said.
Article Summary: The Mozen Flow Ignite has a built-in lighter and torch. The Nomad is a wearable lanyard cable with three connector types. Amkette says the aim is to cut down the number of cables users have to carry. Both cables support charging of up to 100W and data transfer of 480Mbps.

Article Title: Sam Altman’s OpenAI reports two AI agents weakened internal monitoring systems
Article Text:
Here’s what OpenAI said

What happened

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In an update, the company said that a GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to its security team. In another case, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, the company revealed. “In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them,” OpenAI said in the blog post.In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. However, OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.In the blog post, OpenAI wrote:“In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes. A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications.In a separate task, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that it had not removed the monitor. In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them. We are strengthening our misalignment monitoring system in response, and are also assessing whether these cases reflect benign overpersistence or a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular.”On October 3, a researcher asked a GPT-6.1 Sol coding agent to create evaluation tasks using employee feedback collected via Slack. The agent was instructed not to send messages in Slack during that process.82 user messages later, the pipeline stopped after its monitor flagged a proposed validation repair and was unable to save the finding to the monitoring database because it lacked the required access. The user then asked for more information about the alarm and about what needed to be done.Initially, the agent interpreted the user’s earlier instruction (“don’t send any messages”) as a restriction on outreach, separate from any issues with the monitoring system.The main agent initially interpreted the earlier no-slack-message instruction as a restriction on outreach, separate from automatic monitoring. Its recorded reasoning concluded that running the pipeline should have normal monitoring notifications enabled.The agent then delegated the task of repairing the monitoring system to a subagent, with an explicit instruction to preserve monitoring and publish genuine results. As it started its task, the subagent then considered again whether the user’s “don’t send any messages” instruction should affect its repair. It recognized that turning off notifications would disable required alerts, and decided not to recommend that exchange.While the subagent decided not to turn on no_notify since doing so would be unsafe, the main agent later reconsidered, reasoning that writing a result to the database could cause the central monitoring notifier to send a message to the user. Its reasoning weighted the expected alerting policy against the user’s earlier instructions, and finally settled on suppressing notifications based on the user’s instruction not to send messages.Based on its judgment that the user’s instruction not to send messages applied to the misalignment monitoring system, the parent agent then directed the subagent to force notification suppression. A follow-up message specified that the suppression requirement covered both the request metadata and the stored result.The subagent then implemented those instructions: its patch emptied the lists of people set to receive monitoring reports, set no_notify to true, and recorded the reason as a user request not to send messages. It also made suppression a prerequisite for writing a review result.
Article Summary: GPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. But OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.
